header.service: DEMO — UC San Diego Athletics Fan & Revenue Lifecycle
header.scope: First contact with Triton athletics → Renewal, lapse, or a first Triton Athletic Fund gift
header.others: Marketing & fan engagement; ticket operations; game-day operations; the Triton Athletic Fund; a central Advancement development officer

journeys.person: A local fan attending their first Triton basketball game, who becomes a season-ticket holder and then a first-time Triton Athletic Fund donor

stages.name: Awareness

doing.value: Hears about a game through a friend, a social post, or a schedule they stumble across; is not on any list yet.

wants.value: A reason to go, on a night that works, without much research.

touchpoints.value: Social feeds; the schedule page; word of mouth; a campus or community email if they happen to be on one.

thinkingFeeling.value: "I didn't know we had a game — is it any good?"

waitingFor.value: Nothing. Nobody is waiting on the institution here, which is why this stage is invisible in the data.

effortWhy.value: Low, and almost entirely self-directed; the institution has no record that this person exists yet.

stages.duration: Weeks to years before a first purchase; unmeasured

stages.name: First purchase

doing.value: Buys a single-game ticket on their phone; the ticket lands in their wallet app and an account is created for them.

wants.value: To buy in under two minutes and know the seat is fine.

touchpoints.value: Ticketing platform on mobile; confirmation email; digital wallet.

thinkingFeeling.value: "That was easy" — the purchase is the smoothest step in the whole map.

effortWhy.value: Low. Purchase is the one step that works end to end; its cost is that the record it creates never leaves the ticketing platform.

stages.duration: Minutes; typically days to a week before the game

stages.name: Game day

doing.value: Transfers one of their two tickets to whoever is coming with them, arrives, scans in, buys something at the concession stand.

wants.value: To get in quickly and have a good night.

touchpoints.value: Digital wallet; gate scanners; concessions; the venue itself.

thinkingFeeling.value: "This was fun — I'd come back." The experience is the strongest asset in the lifecycle.

effortWhy.value: Low for the fan. The cost sits on the institution's side: the scan records a barcode, not a person, so the best evidence of interest anywhere in the lifecycle is discarded at the door.

stages.duration: One evening; roughly three hours in the building

stages.name: After the game

doing.value: Receives a thank-you and a next-game offer at the account that bought the tickets; the person who attended on the transferred ticket receives nothing.

wants.value: To be recognised as someone who came, and told about the next one worth going to.

thinkingFeeling.value: "Why am I being asked to buy a ticket I already bought?"

effortWhy.value: Low effort, but this is where the relationship is quietly lost: the follow-up is aimed at the buyer of record rather than at the people who were actually there.

stages.duration: 24–72 hours after the game, then a campaign cadence of every one to two weeks

stages.name: Renewal or a first gift

doing.value: Renews as a season-ticket holder in the spring, then receives a Triton Athletic Fund letter days later and makes a first small gift.

wants.value: To keep the seats and — if they give — to be thanked promptly and asked once.

touchpoints.value: Renewal invoice; Fund solicitation letter; gift form; the receipt, eventually.

thinkingFeeling.value: "You just asked me for money." The two asks read as one institution failing to keep track of itself.

waitingFor.value: A receipt and acknowledgment — which took about six weeks.

effortWhy.value: High, and the highest in the map: this is the point where both the systems and the units change, and the fan absorbs the seam.

stages.duration: Renewal window ~4 weeks in spring; Fund solicitation days later; receipt ~6 weeks after the gift

stages.name: Lapse and win-back

doing.value: Stops buying — usually without saying so — and is either worked in a post-season win-back campaign or is not.

wants.value: Either a reason to come back or to be left alone; not to be worked as a stranger after five years of seats.

touchpoints.value: Win-back email, if it runs; renewal reminders that simply stop.

thinkingFeeling.value: "I guess I just stopped going." Lapse is rarely a decision the fan announces.

waitingFor.value: Nothing. Lapse is silent, which is why it is discovered late.

effortWhy.value: Moderate for the fan, high variance for the institution: whether a lapsed buyer is worked at all depends on available staff time rather than on who they were.

stages.duration: Discovered a season late; win-back run once, after the season

momentsThatMatter.why: It is the only part of the lifecycle the fan describes without complaint, and the strongest evidence of interest the institution ever gets — and it is recorded as a count.

momentsThatMatter.moment: The renewal invoice and the Fund letter arriving days apart (stage 5)
momentsThatMatter.why: It is where the fan decides whether this is one relationship or two transactions, and the moment the institution's internal structure becomes visible to them.

dropoutPoints.what: The person who attended on a transferred ticket is never contacted, so an interested attendee leaves no trace and is never asked back.
Buyers stop without notice and are discovered a season later; win-back is then worked in spreadsheet order until staff time runs out.

journeys.person: DEMO (illustrative): Athletics staff running the basketball season, across marketing, ticket and event operations, and the Fund (composite of INT-2 to INT-4)

doing.value: Ticket operations recommends the price tiers and the Athletics Director signs off. Marketing builds the season's audience segments by hand: last season's buyers, single-game buyers, students, lapsed.

thinkingFeeling.value: "Which segment gets which offer and when is my call, and it's mostly instinct and last year's numbers." (INT-2)

effortWhy.value: Segments are built by hand from last season's lists (INT-2).

doing.value: Exports purchase history from the ticketing platform and re-uploads it to the email platform before every campaign, then picks the segment, the offer, and the send date.

thinkingFeeling.value: "by the time it's in my hands it's a week old." (INT-2)

waitingFor.value: The export, which is a week old when it arrives.

effortWhy.value: Every campaign starts with a manual export and re-upload (INT-2).

doing.value: Builds the comp list in a spreadsheet the week of the game and keeps comps out of the marketing audience; pushes the manifest to the scanners.

thinkingFeeling.value: "The comp list is its own mess." (INT-3)

effortWhy.value: Staff, recruits, and community groups all arrive as comps, and the list is built by hand each week (INT-3).

doing.value: Scans people in. The platform records the scan against the barcode, and a transferred ticket no longer points to the buyer.

thinkingFeeling.value: "We know how many people came through. We do not know, account by account, who was in the building." (INT-3)

effortWhy.value: The scan works; what it records is a barcode, not a person (INT-3).

doing.value: Marketing gets scans back as a gate count, not accounts. Ticket operations pulls the season-ticket holder file and emails it to the Fund, usually once a month.

thinkingFeeling.value: "if I'm asking 'did the people I emailed come back', I can't answer that." (INT-2)

waitingFor.value: Attendance by account, which never arrives (marketing); the monthly file (the Fund).

effortWhy.value: Each unit waits on a file another unit sends by hand (INT-2, INT-3, INT-4).

doing.value: The Fund picks who to approach and at what amount from the monthly export. Gifts go to central Advancement for processing and receipting on a batch cycle. Clearance for an assigned prospect often comes after the letter has gone out.

touchpoints.value: Season-ticket holder file; central Advancement CRM; letters

thinkingFeeling.value: "I've had donors call me about a receipt I can't produce." (INT-4)

waitingFor.value: Receipts from central gift processing; clearance from central Advancement.

effortWhy.value: The ask runs on a weeks-old file and on clearance that arrives late (INT-4, INT-5).

doing.value: Runs win-back off a spreadsheet after the season.

thinkingFeeling.value: "whether it happens at all depends on whether I have a student worker that month." (INT-2)

waitingFor.value: A student worker to run it.

effortWhy.value: The work depends on whether there is someone to do it that month (INT-2).
